title: A project with its own process keeps it
what: an existing game whose CLAUDE.md and project skills define its process and that has no studio docs/ROADMAP.md: follow the project's process and skills (build, tests, maps); use the studio's references only as a reference, never bootstrap or init.sh unless the director asks to adopt the studio
when: the studio triggers inside a game made before it, e.g. Zombolic (ship skill, autotest.sh, its own roadmap)
why: installed globally, its description matches every co-op Unity game, so 'rebuild and test' in Zombolic could pull it in instead of the ship skill

title: Editor steps must not create temp objects in the active scene
what: Editor steps make their temporary GameObjects (prefab building, generated roots) in a throwaway additive scene or set the target scene active first; Builder.BuildPlayer refuses when an open scene is dirty instead of building.
when: any idempotent editor step or build run by eval in a shared editor
why: CreatePrimitive/new GameObject in eval lands in the director's active scene and marks it modified; BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer in Unity 6.3 then shows a modal 'Scene(s) Have Been Modified' that blocks the shared editor until eval times out (25 min lost in Trolley phase 3).

title: NGO prefabs saved by script keep GlobalObjectIdHash 0 on disk
what: After PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAsset of a NetworkObject prefab, AssetDatabase.ForceReserializeAssets(path) and read the hash back from the file; fail the step if it is 0.
when: editor steps that build network prefabs
why: NetworkObject.OnValidate fills the id in memory only; the build gets it but the file shows 0, so hook/reviews diff nothing and a re-save rewrites ids.

title: Generated concepts only after the board, with the liked references attached
what: In phase 2 show the board of real references first. Order generated concept sheets only after the director has marked likes and not-its, attach the liked frames to the generator and list the not-its in the brief. Curate Steam screenshots by eye before the board: the first ones are often menus and aerial views.
when: Any style or character choice where an image generator is available.
why: Two rounds of generated sheets made from a written brief were rejected as stock (the generator falls back to one soft cute 3D look). With seven liked reference frames attached, the next sheets were liked at once and the director chose a cast two boards later.

title: Measure the pace of emergent crowd events with a headless shift sim before tuning
what: Before changing the numbers of an emergent rule (brawls, panics, queues), run the crowd simulation without a scene for a whole session with the real door/waves and a simple model of players (supply every N s, reaction to events) and print events per session, peak and mean at once, share of time, damage. Compare variants side by side; then freeze the chosen numbers into a logic test (events per session in a band).
when: a playtest says an emergent event happens too often or too rarely
why: BlackFriday PT-3: the brawl rule looked fine per shelf but a 600 s sim showed 159 brawls a shift and 18 clouds at once; four rule variants were compared in minutes, the pick is guarded by a logic test

title: Editor physics labs must clear the dirty flag of DynamicsManager
what: An editor tool that sets Physics.simulationMode = Script for Physics.Simulate marks ProjectSettings/DynamicsManager.asset dirty even when it restores the mode; the next save (a player build) rewrites the file in the new serialized format. In the tool's finally: restore the mode and EditorUtility.ClearDirty every object of AssetDatabase.LoadAllAssetsAtPath(ProjectSettings/DynamicsManager.asset).
when: writing an editor-side physics test bench (ragdolls, throws) that steps physics by hand
why: BlackFriday PT-3: a ragdoll lab left a 40-line DynamicsManager diff after the build

title: Model orders: measured budgets, a compare sheet and an independent re-import
what: When ordering models from a generator agent (Codex with headless Blender): take triangle budgets from a measurement of what the game draws now, not from a guess; give stylised props their exaggerated sizes in the brief; require a side-by-side sheet with the approved concept and PASS or FAIL against each limit; then re-import every FBX yourself with a small Blender script before believing the report.
when: Any batch of generated 3D models before it goes to Unity.
why: The agent reported 'checks passed' with twice the stated triangle limit and built a box into the staff mesh; my own 500-triangle limit was a guess, while the prototype's character has about 1,400. Props built to realistic sizes came out thin and needed two more passes; the compare sheet made each gap obvious in one look.

title: In a game with a settled look, ask the director for their own references before direction cards
what: When a new place or feature is designed inside a game whose look is already set, first ask the director for 2-3 pictures of what they imagine; build direction cards only if they have none, and then from the game's own style (its packs and build shots) rather than from photos of real places and other media.
when: phase 5-6 content cards: a hub, a base, a new map area; not phase 2 of a new game
why: Zombolic hub redesign 2026-11-20: four directions from real photos (Soviet industrial zone, container walls, castles, our checkpoint) were rejected as a whole («Все не то»); the director answered with three cartoon pictures of a lived-in survivors' camp and the work went on from those.
source: Zombolic, hub for the shelter siege

title: Baked binary .asset files must be marked binary in .gitattributes
what: The common Unity .gitattributes template sets '*.asset ... eol=lf' without 'text'; git then converts line endings without looking at the content, so a CR LF pair inside a baked binary NavMesh drops a byte and Unity refuses to load the file ('Unknown error occurred while loading'). Mark baked binary assets binary ('*NavMesh.asset binary', 'NavMesh-*.asset binary', 'LightingData.asset binary') and add a pre-commit check: a staged .asset whose blob has a NUL byte in its first 8000 bytes while git check-attr says text=set, or text unspecified with eol set, blocks the commit. A Unity binary serialized file declares its size in the header (offset 24, 8 bytes big-endian for format >= 22): compare it with the blob size to find already-damaged files.
when: phase 0 (template .gitattributes) and whenever a build log shows 'Unknown error occurred while loading' for a baked asset
why: Zombolic: City_NavMesh.asset in master was 2 bytes short of its header; every fresh checkout and every build lost the city's navigation until the intact file was found in the checkout that baked it

title: A boring or empty map is a space problem first
what: When a playtest calls a map empty, easy or 'did the task and left', measure the space - size, street widths, sightlines against the AI sight range, relief, routes, respite - before proposing a mechanic, an AI rule or a balance change.
when: after a playtest or a director's remark that a map is boring; before writing any design fix for it
why: The studio answered such a playtest with director rules and a new raid structure; the director rejected it: the cause was big spaces, wide straight streets and far idle AI.
source: Zombolic, playtest 2026-11-21, GDD 1.7 section 2 and docs/ld_pilot (commit a80cd1a1)

title: Level design rules come from the game's own numbers
what: Derive map limits from balance data: sightlines from the AI sight range, map size and respite spacing from sprint speeds, relief steps from jump height, safe fall and the kit's storey; three street widths, three routes overlapping at most a third, respite buildings with two real exits; every story place read in three layers and given a passport before dressing; one legend per map.
when: phase 6, designing any new map or reworking one
why: A map built without these numbers was flat, wide and empty; with them a draft could be checked and argued in metres instead of taste.
source: Zombolic, playtest 2026-11-21, GDD 1.7 section 2 and docs/ld_pilot (commit a80cd1a1)

title: What breaks a sightline: tall staggered blockers, offsets with a building, walls at the street
what: Cars do not block sight (the eye is above the roof) - buses, lorries, tents, blind fences and houses do; one blocker across a street is not enough, two staggered ones are; a street offset needs its width plus a building; walls stand right at the street; the vehicle's street is broken only by a bend.
when: laying out streets and blockers on a map scheme or a gray build
why: The first layout with straight streets and a traffic jam of cars measured 100 m of open view; it took these five changes to reach 40 m.
source: Zombolic, playtest 2026-11-21, GDD 1.7 section 2 and docs/ld_pilot (commit a80cd1a1)

title: Map scheme from one coordinate table, checked by script before anything is built
what: Draw a new map as one JSON table (levels, ramps, streets, buildings at real footprints and doors, tall and low blockers, routes, spawns) and run scripts/map-scheme.py: two to-scale sheets plus checks of route length and overlap, distance to a respite door and the longest sightline. Iterate the layout against the checks; the director approves the sheets before a gray build.
when: phase 6, step 'scheme' of the map cycle; also to show a director a layout without opening Unity
why: The check found what the eye missed: 100 m sightlines, cars that hide nothing, respite houses whose second door opened onto a fenced yard.
source: Zombolic, playtest 2026-11-21, GDD 1.7 section 2 and docs/ld_pilot (commit a80cd1a1)
